title: fix(core): the unknown-key warning drops a retired reason and points at the interface file
body:
Fixes #5642

The dev-mode unknown-key warning printed two things that had outlived the change
they described — a **retired reason** and a **wrong file path** — in prose that
reaches an author's console and prescribes an edit.

## Before / after

```diff
-      'check for a typo, or promote the key to an explicit field on `ActionDef` ' +
-      '(packages/core/src/actions/actionKeys.ts). Warned rather than rejected because `ActionDef` ' +
-      'still carries `[key: string]: any`, so the compiler cannot see this (objectstack#4075).',
+      'check for a typo, or promote the key to an explicit field on `ActionDef` ' +
+      '(packages/core/src/actions/ActionRunner.ts), adding it to `ACTION_DEF_KEYS` ' +
+      '(packages/core/src/actions/actionKeys.ts) in the SAME commit — the pin test derives one ' +
+      'from the other, so either edit alone goes red. Warned rather than rejected because `tsc` ' +
+      'only sees actions authored in code: this one may have arrived as DATA, and stored ' +
+      '`sys_metadata` rows reach the runner unparsed (objectstack#3903).',
```

## Both premises verified on today's `origin/main` (merge base `eddc1dd97`)

**Half 1 — the stated reason is false.** `ActionDef` is declared at
`packages/core/src/actions/ActionRunner.ts:112` and ends at `:440`; the only
index signatures in that file are at `:63` (`ActionContext`, lines 56-64) and
`:584` (`ActionParamOption`, lines 581-585) — none inside `ActionDef`. The
strongest evidence is the pin test's own verdict, `actionKeys.pin.test.ts:108`:

```ts
    expect({
      ActionDef: hasIndexSignature('ActionDef'),
      ActionContext: hasIndexSignature('ActionContext'),
    }).toEqual({ ActionDef: false, ActionContext: true });
```

which passes today: `✓ ActionDef has NO index signature, and ActionContext still does 86ms`.
`actionDef-closed-surface.test.ts` pins the same fact from the compiler's side
(`// @ts-expect-error - `targt` is a typo for `target``, which would go red in the
*unused-directive* direction if the key were accepted again).

The replacement reason is not invented for this PR: it is the one the module's
own header already gives for why this warning survived step 3 — the two
mechanisms cover **disjoint populations**. `tsc` sees action literals authored in
code; the warning sees actions that arrive as **data**, from stored
`sys_metadata` rows rehydrated unparsed (objectstack#3903). The file now says one
thing.

**Half 2 — the prescription named the wrong file.** The message sent an author
editing the *interface* to `actionKeys.ts`, which holds the *inventory*
(`ACTION_DEF_KEYS`). That half-change is exactly what the pin test reddens on:
it re-derives the inventory from the interface's AST and reports
`{ missing, stale }`, so the inventory-only edit fails as `stale`. The new text
names `ActionRunner.ts` for the field, `ACTION_DEF_KEYS` as the same-commit
second edit, and says why.

**Every path and symbol in the new message resolves** — verified, and now pinned
(see the second new test): `packages/core/src/actions/ActionRunner.ts` contains
`export interface ActionDef {`; `packages/core/src/actions/actionKeys.ts`
contains `export const ACTION_DEF_KEYS`.

## Same-root prose swept in the same pass

The card asked for the two stale comments in the pin test; two more in
`actionKeys.ts` itself carried the same retired claim in the present tense and
are named here rather than left to rot:

| Where | Retired claim | Now |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `actionKeys.ts` — `warnOnUnknownActionKeys`'s JSDoc | "the compiler cannot help **while the index signature stands**. Until it comes down, this is the audible half." | compiler catches it in code-authored literals (step 3); this is the audible half for the data-borne population |
| `actionKeys.ts` — `ACTION_DEF_KEYS`' JSDoc | "`keyof ActionDef` cannot substitute for this list: **the index signature widens it to `string \| number`**" | types are erased before anything runs, so `keyof` hands a runtime classifier nothing |
| `actionKeys.pin.test.ts` header | "its **`[key: string]: any` widens `keyof` to `string \| number`** — so the list is data" | interface and its `keyof` are both erased — so the list is data (conclusion unchanged) |
| `actionKeys.pin.test.ts` — the `targt` case | "`targt` **type-checks today: ActionDef's index signature accepts it**" | no longer type-checks in a literal (closed-surface test pins the rejection); still invisible in the data population this warning serves |

Sweep result stated either way: the file's other three console messages were
checked — the retired-key branch prints `RETIRED_ACTION_KEYS[key]` (a rename
prescription, no index-signature claim) and `warnOnDeprecatedObjectParams`'s
message is about `params`/`bodyExtra`. Neither repeats the retired claim, so
neither is touched. Repo-wide, the only other prose naming
`actions/actionKeys.ts` (`app-shell/.../predicate.ts:180`,
`core/src/evaluator/rowPredicateCanon.ts:184`,
`core/src/utils/dashboard-filters.ts:198`, two script files) points at that file
for `warnOnUnknownActionKeys` / the dev gate — which really do live there — so
those pointers are correct and stay.

## The message text is now pinned

Nothing asserted this message's tail, which is how it rotted. Two new tests in
`actionKeys.pin.test.ts`:

- `sends the author to the interface, and drops the reason step 3 retired` — a
  three-way object assertion, so a regression names which half broke.
- `the file path it prints really declares the interface it prescribes` —
  resolves the paths **off the printed message** and reads the files, so a move
  or rename reddens by name instead of shipping a second dead prescription. (A
  fix for a wrong pointer must not install another one.)

**Reverse verification** (ablation, on the committed fix, restore via an `EXIT`
trap): re-injecting the old message tail and re-running the pin test —
mutation confirmed on disk before the run (`grep -c` on the injected text `1`,
on the removed text `0`) — turns both new tests red and nothing else:

```
 × sends the author to the interface, and drops the reason step 3 retired
-   "namesTheSecondEdit": true,          +   "namesTheSecondEdit": false,
-   "pointsAtTheInterfaceFile": true,    +   "pointsAtTheInterfaceFile": false,
-   "repeatsTheRetiredIndexSignature": false,  +   "repeatsTheRetiredIndexSignature": true,
 × the file path it prints really declares the interface it prescribes
-   "declaringPaths": ["packages/core/src/actions/ActionRunner.ts"]  +   "declaringPaths": []
      Tests  2 failed | 17 passed (19)
```

No rebuild was needed for either leg and none was run: the pin test imports the
subject as `from '../actionKeys'` — a relative **source** specifier that never
resolves through the package's `exports` to `dist/`, so there is no stale-artifact
path here. Restore leg confirmed on disk afterwards (new text count `1`, retired
claim count `0`, `git diff` empty against the commit).

## No behaviour change

`classifyActionKeys`, `KNOWN_ACTION_KEYS`, `ACTION_DEF_KEYS` and its derivation
are untouched; the warning fires on exactly the same actions, once per
(action, problem), and stays silent in production. Only the printed prose moved.

## Verification — all on `ef08b2453`, the final commit

| Leg | Verdict line |
| --- | --- |
| `pnpm --filter '@object-ui/core^...' build` | `os-verify-lock: VERDICT command-exit 0 · held the lock 8s` |
| `pnpm vitest run` (3 action-key test files) | `Test Files  3 passed (3)` / `Tests  59 passed (59)`, exit `0` |
| `pnpm --filter @object-ui/core type-check` | `> @object-ui/core@17.6.0 type-check` → `tsc --noEmit && tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`, `VERDICT command-exit 0` |
| `pnpm --filter @object-ui/core lint` | `VERDICT command-exit 0` — 191 files, 0 errors, 0 warnings on both changed files |
| `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs` | `✅  2 source file(s) of 1 released package(s) changed, and this change declares 1 changeset(s)` |
| `node scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs` | `✅  No changeset declares a `major` bump.` |
| `node scripts/check-changeset-fixed.mjs` | `✅  All workspace packages are in the changeset fixed group.` |
| `node scripts/check-control-bytes.mjs` | `✅  check-control-bytes: OK (scanned 4901 tracked text file(s); skipped 85 binary).` |
| `node scripts/check-action-forward-parity.mjs` | `✅  action forward parity: 5 surfaces checked against 39 runtime-read keys from 4 consumers` |
| `node scripts/check-lint-coverage.mjs` | `✅  lint coverage: 46/46 packages linted, 0 with outstanding errors (0 total).` |
| `node scripts/check-type-check-coverage.mjs` | `✅  type-check coverage: 45/46 via `type-check` … 0 errors outstanding` |

Every exit code above was captured before any pipe (`cmd > log 2>&1; EXIT=$?`),
and each verdict line is the one the gate printed itself.

**Declared lint narrowing.** Lint ran over `packages/core` (the package's own
`eslint .`, i.e. exactly what `turbo run lint` runs for it) rather than the whole
monorepo. Three pieces of evidence that this excludes nothing: (1) the population
comes from ESLint's own config resolution, not from a hand-picked file list;
(2) the count is read from `--format json` — 191 files, 0 errors; (3) the config
is **not** type-aware — `eslint.config.js` extends `tseslint.configs.recommended`
(not `recommendedTypeChecked`) and its `languageOptions` declares no
`parserOptions.project` / `projectService`, so a file's verdict depends only on
its own text plus shared config, neither of which this diff touches outside
`packages/core`. CI runs the whole farm regardless.

`scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs` does not exist in this repo and the framework
copy is bound to its own checkout (run from this worktree it reported "this
branch changes nothing against 'origin/main' (merge base 95437e7d2)" — the
framework's base), so the gate family above was derived by hand from the three
changed paths.
